analysis:
The supplied units are base text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md; the PR is documentation-only per the patch excerpt (a date bump, a new stop-drain paragraph near head lines 926-932, and revised status bullets near head lines 998-1013). No code or controls are changed in the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete security regression.

The new stop/drain paragraph describes an unverified behavior. With the coordinator connection down and no unfinished work, the drain finishes after 10 seconds without a coordinator acknowledgement. Shutdown then waits 15 seconds per model unload and leaves a model whose native retirement never finishes to process exit. This touches T-053 (stale authorization surviving connection change), T-028 (residual GPU memory and KV data) and TB-002 (coordinator WebSocket). The claim that 'nothing queued can still reach the coordinator' and the process-exit cleanup of un-retired models are implementation contracts in ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown and ServiceDrain.swift, which were not supplied. They need confirming there: unfinished usage must not be lost or billed incorrectly, and the unload timeout must not leave decrypted prompts or KV cache resident beyond process exit. I could not verify them, so I record them as an open integration question rather than a finding.

The status-bullet change (the 'Configuration change needs a restart' diff of enabled_models) is only partly visible, since the patch excerpt is truncated. It appears to be a display change in StatusCommand and does not touch the T-041 prefix-cache surface. The base text confirms the prefix-cache status vocabulary and 'Model names and exact load figures remain private' in the logs, and I saw no weakening of that.

The rest of the supplied base text is unchanged context: the logs refusal lines, the report upload, and the logout and unenroll semantics. It shows no new attack surface in this diff.
